what_happened: Both arms crashed deterministically during training: one DDP rank raised the model's strict finite-positive-measure validation and its peers hung in ALLREDUCE (the incident that motivated the step failure barrier, commit 1503b853). No gate quantity, resolution-sweep value, or validation comparison was ever computed.

diagnosis.raw_data: All 484 DrivAerML vehicle surfaces scanned: zero cells with non-positive or non-finite fp32 area (per-case minima 1.4e-11 to 2.3e-9).
diagnosis.mechanism: The z-rotation augmentation recomputes areas from rotated fp32 points; on sliver cells this erodes the computed area by up to 5770x in a 16-angle probe (run_44: 1.38e-11 raw -> 2.39e-15 rotated), i.e. to the edge of fp32 subnormal. Continuous training-time angles across 500 epochs x 484 cases make an exact-zero draw inevitable; the model's measure validation then rightly rejects the sample.
diagnosis.artifact: area_scan.jsonl in the HSG task dir (484 rows, per-case raw and rotated minima).

amendment.augment: true -> false for BOTH arms (the rotation augmentation was incidental to the registered question and is the failure mechanism; it also restores the historical no-augmentation protocol)
amendment.mixedres_draw_location: moves from the augmentation slot to the transform chain (replacing the fixed SubsampleMesh); validation batches therefore also draw random resolutions, which affects monitoring only -- every registered gate reads the final-checkpoint resolution sweep
amendment.restart: all four lanes restart from epoch 0 under the amended protocol; the 87/73/210/153 epochs trained under augment=true are discarded rather than mixed into a heterogeneous-protocol run
amendment.unchanged: arms, seeds, model, epochs, learning rate, precision, instrument, and every deciding gate of the preregistration
